text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday's Slovenian newspapers.
- Centre-left Liberal Democrat Janez Drnovsek narrowly won a second term as Prime Minister after the Slovenian parliament on Thursday voted by 46 to 44 in his favour.
- Slovenian political parties accused each other of corrupt dealings in an effort to gain an extra vote in Thursday's parliamentary vote for prime minister.

- Slovenia's Ministry of Economic Affairs said presidency over the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) would not be an easy task. One of the hardest tasks for Slovenia will be promotion of CEFTA in the U.S. and Far East.
- Slovenia's Ecological Fund has made available 710 million tolars ($4.96 million) for loans for environmentally-friendly construction.
- Janez Drnovsek has to name ministers of the new government in 15 days, and seven days later his proposed candidates must attend a parliamentary hearing.
- Slovenian Railways' losses last year reached three billion tolars ($21.1 million), mostly due to a fall in the number of cargo transports.

- The first trading days of the year proved foreign investors were not inhibited by the uncertain political situation in Slovenia, which was left without a government after inconclusive elections on November 10, analysts said.
